fix: properly kill frontend dev server on dev shell exit

The previous trap only killed the shell script wrapper (frontend-dev),
leaving the bun/vite child process alive. This caused the shell to hang
on exit because the background job was still running.

Now we:
- disown the background job so bash doesn't wait for it
- kill the entire process group (wrapper + bun + vite)
- force-kill after 0.5s as a fallback

fix: use exec in dev subshell so kill -9 hits bun directly

The previous attempts tried to kill a devenv script wrapper process,
which left bun/vite alive as orphaned children. Since devenv scripts
add a shell wrapper around the command, 0 was the wrapper's PID —
not bun's.

Now we run (cd frontend && exec bun run dev) &, which replaces the
subshell with bun. 0 is bun's PID directly, so kill -9 terminates
the actual dev server. No ps/pgrep/process-group tricks needed.

fix: register HEAD routes for media serving to support Meta/Threads scraper

so these requests were returning 405 Method Not Allowed, causing Threads
image uploads to fail.

fix: add Content-Length header to media serving for Meta/Threads scraper

fix: add robots.txt endpoint and document IPv6 requirement for Threads

Also added documentation note about IPv6 AAAA record requirement for
Threads image uploads to work correctly.

fix: register HEAD route for robots.txt

fix: use http.ServeContent for media serving to support Range requests

Meta's scraper sends Range requests to verify files before downloading.
c.Stream() ignores Range headers and returns 200 OK with full file,
causing Meta to abort. http.ServeContent automatically handles Range
requests, returns 206 Partial Content, and injects Accept-Ranges header.

fix(posts): cancel jobs by type + json_extract, not payload LIKE

The previous query (`WHERE payload LIKE '%<postID>%'`) matched any job
whose payload contained the post UUID as a substring, not just the
publish_post job for that post. A media_cleanup or refresh_token job
whose payload embedded the post ID in a free-text field (or a future
job type that uses the post_id JSON key) would have been silently
cancelled along with the real job, leaving the post scheduled forever.

Replaced with `type = ? AND json_extract(payload, '$.post_id') = ?`,
which is strictly more precise. Added a regression test that
constructs a jobs table with five jobs (target, other-post,
substring-decoy, prefix-decoy, non-publish-decoy) and asserts only the
target is deleted.

fix(oauth): make callback redirects absolute URLs

The error and success redirects in OAuthHandler returned relative paths
(`/accounts?error=...`, `/accounts/callback?status=success&...`),
which 404 behind any reverse proxy that doesn't add the path prefix,
or that the SPA is served on a subpath.

Pass the FrontendURL into the handler and prefix both redirects with
it (trailing slash stripped, idempotent on the input).

fix(config): derive OAuth redirect URIs from OPENPOST_APP_URL

The previous Go defaults hardcoded `http://localhost:8080/api/v1/.../callback`
for X, LinkedIn, Threads — and the .env.example pointed at
`http://localhost:5173/.../callback`. Neither matched the value the
operator actually deployed at, so OAuth callbacks 404'd or were
rejected with `redirect_uri_mismatch` until the operator manually set
all three *_REDIRECT_URI env vars.

Added `oauthRedirectFromFrontend(primary, alias, frontend, path)` that
prefers an operator-set *_REDIRECT_URI (or its alias) when present
and otherwise returns `${frontend}${path}`. The Mastodon redirect
still defaults to the OOB flow (`urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob`),
matching the existing .env.example and not requiring a real callback
URL.

Rewrote .env.example comments to make the dependency on
OPENPOST_APP_URL explicit and to mark each *_REDIRECT_URI as
optional.

Added unit tests for the helper covering: explicit env, alias
fallback, derive-from-frontend, trailing slash, no-alias case, and
empty-frontend edge case.

chore(lint): extract repeated string literals to named constants

`golangci-lint run` was reporting 13 goconst issues (every
`Severity: "error" / "warning" / Provider: "<platform>"" site in
the platform adapters, plus the 5 `"published"` post-status
checks scattered across the handlers and the publisher). The values
are stable contracts — the Severity strings are part of the JSON
schema consumed by the frontend, and the provider strings must
match the canonical provider keys documented in AGENTS.md.

This change is purely a refactor: it adds untyped string constants
in two places

* `internal/platform/constants.go` — severityError, severityWarning,
  providerBluesky/LinkedIn/Mastodon/Threads/X, bskyRecordTypeField,
  jsonFieldVideo
* `internal/models/models.go` — PostStatusDraft/Scheduled/
  Publishing/Published/Failed

and replaces each literal with the named constant. Two
`//nolint:goconst` directives on the published-status checks in
`media.go` and `posts.go` are removed because the checks now use
the constant directly.

`compose-simple.svelte` got a small Prettier reformat (CSS class
ordering inside a Tailwind utility) as a side effect of bringing
the file up to Prettier's expectations. No behaviour change.

feat(auth): first-class API tokens with unified bearer auth

The CLI needs long-lived, revocable credentials. JWTs are fine for
web sessions but wrong for the CLI: short-lived, can't be revoked
before expiry, and the same secret is shared with the browser
localStorage flow. This change adds an opaque-token model alongside
the existing JWT path, and switches the Huma middleware to a
pluggable Authenticator so the two flows coexist.

Data layer
  api_tokens         opaque tokens stored as sha256 hashes. Token
                     format: op_cli_<8-hex-prefix>_<base64url-secret>.
                     The prefix is the first 8 hex of sha256(secret);
                     the hash is the full sha256. We never store or
                     log the raw secret. Default scope 'cli:full'.
                     Default expiry 90 days; null = never for self-
                     hosted. FK-cascades on user delete.

  cli_auth_sessions  device-flow sessions for the next phase. Both
                     the device code and the user code are stored as
                     sha256 hashes; the plain user_code only ever
                     leaves the server inside the verification URL.
                     Status is a CHECK-constrained enum.

  Migration 008 and 009 are idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS) and picked up
  by the auto-embed in migrations.go, matching the 007 pattern.

Auth layer
  The JWT code in services/auth/auth.go is unchanged. A new
  middleware.Authenticator interface wraps it: a JWTAuthenticator
  delegates to the existing *auth.Service, and a CompositeService
  tries JWT first, falls back to API tokens. AuthMiddleware now
  takes the interface instead of *auth.Service. The Echo-native
  JWTMiddleware (used outside the Huma path) is preserved
  byte-for-byte. All Huma-using handlers are mechanically switched
  to the new constructor parameter; the AuthHandler falls back to
  a JWT-only authenticator when no api-tokens service is wired, so
  the change is back-compat.

API surface
  GET    /api/v1/api-tokens        list the caller's tokens
  POST   /api/v1/api-tokens        mint a new token (raw value
                                   returned once, then unrecoverable)
  DELETE /api/v1/api-tokens/{id}   revoke

Service
  internal/services/apitokens implements GenerateToken, HashToken,
  ValidateToken (prefix lookup + hash verify), ListTokens,
  RevokeToken, TouchLastUsedAt. Tests cover happy path, never-
  expiry, expired tokens, invalid prefix, revoked tokens, list
  isolation per user, and the raw token is asserted on by prefix
  only (never logged in full).

feat(auth): CLI device-flow authorization endpoints

The CLI never handles the user's password, TOTP, or passkey. The
device-flow pattern (RFC 8628-style, mapped to a familiar shape) lets
the CLI redirect the user to the web UI for approval and poll for
the resulting API token.

Endpoints (all under /api/v1/cli/auth):
  POST /start        no auth, opens a session; returns device_code,
                     user_code, verification_url, expires_in, interval.
                     Device code and user code are stored as sha256
                     hashes; only the plain user_code ever leaves the
                     server. Rate-limited per client IP.
  POST /poll         no auth, CLI polls with device_code. Returns
                     authorization_pending / approved / access_denied /
                     expired_token, plus the raw token on first
                     successful approval. Enforces a 1s minimum
                     poll interval (last_polled_at) and the
                     session's interval_seconds for Retry-After.
  GET  /session      auth required, looked up by user_code from the
                     URL the user opens. The web approval page needs
                     this to render the request before the user
                     decides.
  POST /approve      auth required, user approves; mints an APIToken
                     via the existing apitokens service and returns
                     once. Default scope cli:full, default expiry 90d.
  POST /deny         auth required, marks the session denied.

New service backend/internal/services/cli_auth wraps the
cli_auth_sessions table. Code allocation retries on user_code hash
collision with a hard cap so we never hand out a duplicate code.
CleanupExpired is exposed for the background worker (wired in a
later change).

Tests cover the happy path, denial, expiry, slow-down, rate limit,
uniqueness, the 'plain user_code is the only thing the CLI gets'
invariant, and the one-shot mint semantics. golangci-lint clean
(httptest.NewRequestWithContext).

Legacy Echo media routes (/api/v1/media/upload, /batch-upload, /metadata)

build(dev): add pre-push lint gate and fix Go toolchain in pre-commit hooks

Two related changes that close the gap where commits that only
touched go.mod / docs / changelogs slipped past the lint suite
and reached CI (or a release) with broken code:

1. Pre-push lint gate. The existing pre-commit hooks only fire
   on staged files matching their `files` regex, so a commit
   that only touches go.mod, the changelog, the docs, or
   docker/Dockerfile doesn't trigger golangci-lint, the same
   way it doesn't get lint-graded in CI's `Run relevant lint
   suite` step. Add scripts/pre-push-lint.sh, which runs the
   same `devenv shell -- lint` suite CI runs and blocks the
   push on any failure. The hook is installed automatically by
   devenv on shell entry (devenv.nix:enterShell). Tag pushes
   skip the local check (CI already gated the commit), and
   OPENPOST_SKIP_PRE_PUSH_LINT=1 is the documented escape
   hatch for already-CI-gated pushes.

2. Pre-commit wrappers now use the pinned Go toolchain. The
   pre-commit hooks invoke /nix/store/.../backend-go-test style
   scripts via `prek`, which doesn't load direnv on its own.
   Without an explicit PATH, those scripts pick up whatever Go
   is on the user's shell, which on a system without direnv
   activation is the OS Go (1.25.9) and doesn't satisfy
   go.mod's `go 1.26.0` minimum. The wrappers now set
   GOROOT and prepend go_1_26 to PATH via runtimeInputs, so
   they work regardless of whether the user is inside the
   devenv shell.

Documented in AGENTS.md alongside the existing commit /
branch / changelog conventions. The `pre-push lint gate is
mandatory` line is explicit about when to run `devenv shell
-- lint` manually and when to use the OPENPOST_SKIP_* escape.

build(dev): pin Go toolchain in pre-commit hook wrappers

The /nix/store/.../backend-go-test style scripts invoked by
pre-commit (via prek) inherit PATH from the calling process,
which doesn't load direnv on its own. Without an explicit Go
on PATH, those scripts pick up the OS Go (1.25.9), which no
longer satisfies go.mod's `go 1.26.0` minimum after the
previous toolchain bump, and fail with:

  go: go.mod requires go >= 1.26.0 (running go 1.25.9;
  GOTOOLCHAIN=local)

Pin go_1_26 via runtimeInputs on the writeShellApplication
calls and export GOROOT so golangci-lint's typecheck uses the
matching standard library. Centralize the package in a
goToolchain let-binding so the languages.go.package and the

fix(schedule): split next-slot from draft-gap overflow to avoid returning non-slot times

The findNextAvailableSlotTime function mixed two semantics: finding the next
configured schedule slot and falling back to last-post + draft-gap-minutes
when all slots on a day were occupied. This caused the 'next slot' endpoint
to return 7:00 AM when the only 6:00 AM slot was already taken, instead of
next week's 6:00 AM.

- Split into findNextConfiguredScheduleSlotTime (real slots only) and
  findNextOverflowPostingTime (explicit overflow utility)
- Updated GetNextAvailableSlot handler to use only configured slots
- Frontend now passes set_id to the next-slot endpoint
- 20 tests covering both functions comprehensively

Add an explicit quick-cut or studio editing mode to the video project
document, raise the project duration ceiling from 20 minutes to 2 hours,
and add a word-level ripple-delete helper that removes a transcript word's

feat(video-studio): add lossless stream-copy quick-cut export

Add a lossless export path that copies encoded source video and audio
packets into MP4 or WebM without transcoding when an edit only removes
kept source ranges. Compatibility is decided from the document (single
supported source, no gaps or composition edits, default presentation),
in points are snapped to and verified against source keyframes, and the
result is re-read to confirm codec and duration before returning.

Also split source artifact generation into an early incomplete index
(keyframes and frame-rate first) followed by a completion pass that adds
the waveform, so long imports stay responsive, and switch long or 4K
sources to a smaller 540p24 hardware-accelerated VP9 proxy profile while
raising the keyframe index limit to 16k.

feat(video-studio): add Quick Cut workflow and Studio editing upgrades

Add an explicit Quick Cut or Full Studio choice on the new-project screen
and in the editor header, with a focused Quick Cut workspace for long
single-source recordings: source-scale kept sections, mark-in/out, split
and remove, keyframe-safe snapping, lossless fast export, and a one-click
move back into Full Studio. Composer handoff always forces Full Studio so
each required format keeps correct dimensions.

Studio upgrades: a resizable timeline, one-click smooth zoom in/out/punch
presets with guided keyframes, word-level transcript ripple deletion that
retimes remaining captions, and recording camera layouts for circle,
rounded, portrait, side-by-side, and full-frame compositions. Timeline
trim and timing gestures are now frame-coalesced so sustained pointer
drags stay responsive.

single video, and open Full Studio with a clean browser console.

fix(admin): make plan overrides actually assign and remove plans

The admin plan override feature shipped in 3.13.0 could never work:
- Assigning a plan failed with a 500 because the generated subscription
  row carried an empty workspace_id that violated the billing_subscriptions
  workspace foreign key. Empty workspace IDs now bind as NULL.
- Every read path only honored paddle subscriptions, so an admin override
  row was invisible to billing status, entitlements, setup state, and
  public profiles. Admin overrides now grant like paid plans everywhere.
- Removing an override from the dialog returned 422 because the documented
  empty plan_id was rejected by minLength validation before the handler
  ran. Empty plan_id now reaches the removal path.

Removal now matches the admin_override_<org> subscription id instead of
the provider label, so overrides remain removable regardless of provider.

Covered by handler and entitlement service tests.

refactor(settings): remove queue spillover gap setting

The "When today's times are full" draft_gap_minutes setting invented
same-day overflow times (last post + gap) when configured slots were
full. That breaks queue semantics - a strict queue should spill to
the next day's next slot, not fabricate a time.

Overflow logic was already dead (findNextOverflowPostingTime removed
in 14e7e56f) but the UI, API, and DB default (60) remained, misleading
users into thinking spillover was active.

Remove the setting end-to-end:
- backend: tombstone DeprecatedDraftGapMinutes, remove from
  Get/Update workspace settings API and column list
- cli: remove DraftGapMinutes field
- frontend: remove WorkspaceSettings field, store handling,
  ScheduleSettingsTab input and help copy, and i18n keys
- messages: drop settings_queue_full / spillover / draft_gap keys
- fixtures: update e2e and cli tests to not expect field
- regenerate openapi.json and types.d.ts

The column stays in the DB as a tombstone for existing installs;
the queue is now strictly slot-based.

fix(queue): block jitter window when finding next slot

Queue was exact-minute only. With +-N random delay a slot 09:00
and a scheduled post at 09:10 with N=15 can jitter to overlap.

Make isSlotOccupied check the jitter window, not just same minute:
- sameMinute still blocks

createSession and every later XRPC call went to https://bsky.social. Resolve
the handle's PDS from its DID document at sign-in, record it as the account's
instance URL, and give each non-default PDS its own adapter keyed like a

accounts keep the default adapter and their existing rows are unchanged, and
the authorization grant's project id is untouched so existing grants still
match on reconnect. Resolution goes through netguard and a failure rejects the
sign-in instead of falling back to the wrong server.

fix(video-editor): isolate animated-image subscriber from effect tracking

A warm-cache subscribe() call invokes its callback synchronously inside the
subscribing effect's tracking context, so the animatedRevision increment fed
back into the effect's own dependencies. Run the callback untracked; media
identity stays tracked in the outer effect.

fix(telemetry): share one bounded chunk recovery policy across surfaces

Replace the divergent app and marketing reload handlers with a single
controller: one decision per failure, persisted per-asset and overall
budgets with no time-window reset, and automatic reloads only with probe
evidence. Editors fall back to the boundary retry while unsaved changes
exist; rejected imports stay rejected.

fix(telemetry): keep deployment context and capture every frontend error

Restore deployment super-properties after identity resets and attach
surface, environment, edition, version, and revision to all exception
captures including buffered ones. Bridge console.error into error
tracking so logged-but-never-thrown failures reach PostHog, and retain
the first-party asset pathname on import failures. Docs now passes its
UI host through like the other surfaces.

fix(build): require explicit PostHog UI host for source-map upload

The US default silently uploaded symbols to the wrong region for EU
projects, leaving production errors unsymbolicated with no build-time
signal. Official builds already pass POSTHOG_UI_HOST explicitly.

fix(themes): patch css-color lookbehind detectors for pre-16.4 Safari

Safari gained regex lookbehind in 16.4, so the pinned

hit api token expiration must be in the future on Create token. Allow

fix(piefed): request post analytics by id (#254)

PieFed's GET /api/alpha/post loads GetPostRequest, which requires an id

content analytics read was rejected with a 422 and PieFed post

fix(piefed): send deleted when deleting a reply (#255)

PieFed's POST /api/alpha/comment/delete loads DeleteCommentRequest, which
requires deleted as well as comment_id; deleted false restores the reply.
The adapter sent only comment_id, so deleting the account's own PieFed
reply was rejected with a 422.

fix(piefed): search communities through the search endpoint (#256)

The destination picker searched PieFed communities with
GET /api/alpha/community/list?search=... . ListCommunitiesRequest has no
search field and excludes unknown ones, so PieFed returned its most
active communities whatever was typed. Search with
GET /api/alpha/search?q=...&type_=Communities, which filters communities
by title and actor ID, as the Lemmy adapter already does.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(piefed): collect nested replies from the post replies tree (#257)

PieFed's GET /api/alpha/post/replies returns a tree: the comments array
holds only top-level comments, and each reply is nested in the replies
array of the comment it answers. The adapter read the top level only, so
replies to comments, including replies to the account's own replies,
never reached the inbox. Walk the tree, listing each comment before its
replies.

fix(piefed): skip moderator-removed replies when listing comments (#258)

When a moderator removes a PieFed reply, the API blanks its body and
reports removed true with deleted false. The adapter skipped only
deleted replies, so a removed reply was stored as a blank inbox comment
and could fire a new-engagement notification. Skip removed replies too,
as the Lemmy adapter already does.

Theory of operation: the scroll container fires scroll events for
vertical movement too, and every event rewrote the viewport state
object, invalidating the waveform plan, filmstrip targets, animated

batches likewise rewrote the visible set even with no membership
change. Both writes are now guarded by pure module-context predicates
so no-op events skip the entire downstream pipeline. No edit math,
layout, gesture, or subscription behavior changes.

fix(peertube): read every page of the channel and comment-thread lists (#265)

Two PeerTube lists were read as a single page. The account's channels
(GET /api/v1/accounts/{name}/video-channels) were requested without
count or start, so PeerTube returned its default page of 15 and
channels past the fifteenth could not be connected or picked, although
the default quota is 20. A video's comment threads were requested as
one page of 100 and never followed start, so on a busy video the older
threads, and new replies on them, never reached the inbox.

Both now go through one helper that requests the largest page PeerTube
accepts and follows start until total.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(peertube): advance the content discovery cursor past every video read (#266)

DiscoverAccountContent pages the channel's videos by offset, but the
next offset was start plus the number of videos kept on the page. Videos
older than the discovery window, or dropped by normalization, did not
count, so the next page started inside the one just read. Once the
window's lower bound was reached no video was kept at all, and the
same cursor came back until the daily read budget ran out. The cycle
never finished, so newer uploads were never discovered.

Advance by every video read, and stop at the first video older than the
window, since the listing is sorted newest first.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(threads): collect nested replies from the conversation edge (#268)

ListComments read GET /{media-id}/replies, which returns only the
top-level replies to a post. A reply to a reply, such as a follower
answering the account's own reply, never reached the inbox. Read
GET /{media-id}/conversation instead, which returns replies at every
depth with the same fields, and thread each one under replied_to.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(facebook): read a post's newest comments first when collecting engagement (#267)

ListComments read one page of GET /{object-id}/comments without an
order. With the default top-level filter the Graph API lists comments
oldest first, so once a post had more comments than one page, every
poll returned the same oldest page and new comments never reached the
inbox. Ask for reverse_chronological order, as the YouTube adapter
already does with order=time.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(community): declare the fixed discovery page size as the minimum (#269)

Lemmy, PieFed, and PeerTube discovery read fixed pages of 20, 20, and
25 and ignore the requested page size, but declared no MinPageSize.
Near the 250-item initial limit the discovery job asks for the smaller
remainder and rejects a page with more items than it asked for, so an
account with more than 250 items in the window failed on the same page
every hour and never finished its initial cycle. Declaring the fixed
size as the minimum lets the job stop at the limit instead, the way it
already does for X.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(media): accept Ogg and M4A uploads the sniffer names differently

container when both subtypes are equal and the sniffed type is audio

subtype aliases onto mp4 before comparing containers.

fix(tiktok): declare and send upload chunks the way TikTok counts them (#306)

TikTok's Media Transfer Guide defines total_chunk_count as video_size
divided by chunk_size rounded down, with the trailing bytes sent in the
final chunk (up to 128 MB), every other chunk 5-64 MB, and a video over
64 MB sent in more than one chunk.

uploadVideoFileToInbox used 64 MiB chunks and rounded the count up, so
any file upload over 64 MiB that was not an exact multiple declared one
chunk more than TikTok's formula and sent the remainder as its own chunk,
down to a few bytes. A 64 MiB + 3 byte video was declared as 2 chunks of
64 MiB (TikTok expects 1) and uploaded as 64 MiB followed by 3 bytes.

Spread the bytes evenly over the fewest chunks that fit the 64 MiB
limit. The count then equals video_size / chunk_size, the remainder is
smaller than the chunk count and rides on the final chunk, and uploads
of 64 MiB or less still go as one chunk.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mastodon): count links as 23 characters and remote mentions by username (#307)

* fix(mastodon): count links as 23 characters and remote mentions by username

Mastodon measures a status after replacing every http(s) link with 23
characters and every @user@domain mention with @user: countableText in
its composer and StatusLengthValidator on the server both do this.
OpenPost counted the raw code points, so a Mastodon post with a long
link was shown as over the limit and failed publishing validation
although Mastodon accepts it: 450 characters and a 100-character link
count as 551 here and 474 on Mastodon.

Apply the same substitutions for Mastodon in capabilities.TextLength
(validation, dynamic limits, generation) and in countPlatformText (the
composer counter), then keep counting code points as Mastodon's composer
does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mastodon): count only links Mastodon recognizes, and keep balanced parentheses

Mastodon only shortens an http(s) link whose host ends in a top-level
domain, so https://intranet/page keeps its literal length there; both
counters now check the host before applying the 23-character rule. The
composer counter also treated the ")" that closes a "(" inside a link
(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)) as trailing punctuation and
counted one character more than the server side, which keeps it.

fix(bluesky): detect hashtags the way Bluesky does (#308)

* fix(bluesky): detect hashtags the way Bluesky does

buildBlueskyFacets matched hashtags with #[A-Za-z0-9_]+, so a tag with a
non-ASCII letter was cut at that letter and published as a different
tag: "#café" became a facet for #caf and "#São_Paulo" one for #S, while
"#日本語" or a tag after a full-width space got no facet at all. It also
linked number-only tags and "#" in the middle of a word ("C#sharp"), and
a tag longer than 64 characters produced a facet longer than the
app.bsky.richtext.facet#tag lexicon allows.

Port TAG_REGEX from @atproto/api's rich-text detection: a tag follows
the start of the text or whitespace (including full-width spaces), runs
to the next space or zero-width character, needs one character that is
not a digit or punctuation, drops trailing punctuation, accepts the
full-width hash, skips the #-keycap emoji and is at most 64 graphemes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(bluesky): leave a hashtag over 640 bytes unlinked

The facet lexicon limits a tag to 640 bytes as well as 64 graphemes, and a
tag of long grapheme clusters (a letter with many combining marks) can pass
the grapheme check and still exceed it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(bluesky): link the whole URL in post facets (#309)

* fix(bluesky): link the whole URL in post facets

blueskyURLPattern took a host that had to end in a dot and at most six
letters before a word boundary, and a path without RFC 3986's sub-delims
",", ";", "!", "'" or "$". A link on a longer top-level domain such as
https://openpost.digital/blog got no link facet at all, and a Google Maps
link (https://www.google.com/maps/@37.5665,126.978,15z) or a Wikipedia
title with a comma was cut at the comma, so Bluesky opened a different
page.

Match the characters a URL can hold unencoded instead, less "*" so
Markdown-style emphasis around a link stays outside it. Characters
outside that set still end the link, so text written straight after a
URL (Japanese without a space, quotes, angle brackets) stays out of it,
and trailing punctuation is still trimmed as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(bluesky): skip a link facet without a host

The wider URL pattern also matches "https:///path" and a bare "https://"
left after trimming, which the old dotted-host pattern never did; neither
is a URI the post record accepts, so no link facet is built for them.

fix(bluesky): skip deleted and system entries when syncing messages (#310)

chat.bsky.convo.getMessages returns a union of messageView,
deletedMessageView (a message the account deleted for itself) and
systemMessageView (group events such as a member joining). FetchMessages
decoded every entry as a message, so the last two, which have no text,
